question_text:
In a game, a player rolls a biased four-sided die. The probability of obtaining each possible score is shown in the table.

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Score} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline \text{Probability} & \frac{1}{12} & k & \frac{1}{4} & \frac{1}{3} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

mark_breakdown.desc: Using the total probability property $\sum P(x_i) = 1$

subparts.solution:
Since this is a probability distribution, $\sum_{i=1}^n P(x_i) = 1$.
$$\therefore \frac{1}{12} + k + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{3} = 1$$
$$\frac{1}{12} + k + \frac{3}{12} + \frac{4}{12} = 1$$
$$k + \frac{8}{12} = 1 \implies k = 1 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For any discrete probability distribution, the sum of all probabilities must equal 1.
step_by_step: Sum the probabilities in the table: $\frac{1}{12} + k + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{3}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Arithmetic errors when adding fractions with different denominators.

subparts.stem: Let the random variable $X$ denote the number of 2s that occur when the die is rolled 2400 times. Calculate the exact mean and standard deviation of $X$.
subparts.solution:
Let $X$ be the number of 2s rolled.
$n = 2400$, so $X = 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots, 2400$, and $p = \frac{1}{3}$ {from a}
$\therefore X \sim \text{B}(2400, \frac{1}{3})$
So, $\mu = np = 2400 \times \frac{1}{3} = 800$
and
$$\sigma = \sqrt{np(1-p)} = \sqrt{2400 \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{2}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{1600}{3}} = \frac{40}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{40\sqrt{3}}{3}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For a binomial random variable $X \sim \text{B}(n, p)$, the mean is $\mu = np$ and standard deviation is $\sigma = \sqrt{np(1-p)}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to rationalize the denominator or taking the variance instead of standard deviation.
